# DesignMD Forge

> A free, offline MCP server for DESIGN.md design-system specs. Search component
> patterns across 290 designs, derive palettes, list official themes, and lint
> your own spec. 11 tools, 4 prompts, no network calls at runtime.

## What this is

DESIGN.md files are plain-text design-system documents (colours, typography,
components, motion) that coding agents read to generate UI matching a target
style. DesignMD Forge bundles 290 of them offline and exposes search and
authoring tools over MCP.

Install: `npx -y designmd-forge` (stdio). A hosted Streamable HTTP connector is
also available.

## Tools

- designmd_search_designs — which brands look like this brief? (category, platform, source, brand, mode, hue)
- designmd_search_sections — who specs a footer, button or nav like this? (group, text, has, position)
- designmd_list_themes — which official theme variants exist? (brand, mode, hue, typeClass)
- designmd_get_design_md — the file, one section, one ### group, a framework flavour, or a theme delta
- designmd_get_guardrails — just the do's and don'ts, at a third of the output
- designmd_list_designs — what exists? (filters, no scoring)
- designmd_list_categories — which category names are valid?
- designmd_lint — structural validation of a draft (0 errors / 0 warnings target)
- designmd_diff — token-level comparison of two specs
- designmd_get_authoring_guide — how to write a DESIGN.md well
- designmd_scaffold_template — a fill-in-the-blank skeleton

## Prompts

- pick-a-design — search → full spec → guardrails, returns a ranked shortlist
- section-inspiration — sections search → read the group, 3–5 candidates plus a synthesis
- theme-pick — list themes → theme delta; says "no themes" when there are none
- author-design-md — guide → scaffold → lint to zero errors and warnings

## What is not covered

- 600 of the 890 markdown files are SwiftUI/Expo/Android flavours and are not indexed.
- 221 of 301 designs have no declared tokens: no facets, no palette.
- Palette filters cover 80 of 301 designs.
- Only Astryx ships official themes; a derived palette is not a theme.
- Prompts are user-invoked templates, not skills.
